value.definition: what the tray puts in place on a machine before it runs

invariants.statement: A worker already on disk is left alone.
A worker download lands under a temporary name before the rename into place.
The startup shortcut is written by PowerShell rather than by Rust.
A startup shortcut already there is left alone.

value.definition: the rotating log file the tray writes its lines to

invariants.statement: A log line has an instant and a level before the message.
The live log is rotated once that log reaches a megabyte.
Three log files are kept.
A log that could not be written is dropped rather than thrown on.
The instant is worked out here rather than drawn from a date library.

value.definition: where the tray program's run begins

invariants.statement: The tray declares every sibling module here.
A tray that replaced itself exits rather than carrying on.
A step that failed is logged and the run carries on.

value.definition: the worker process the tray spawns and spawns again

invariants.statement: A worker that exited on its own is spawned again.
A worker the tray killed is left dead.
The worker is looked at every five hundred milliseconds.
The worker runs with no console window of its own.

value.definition: the notification area icon and the menu behind it

invariants.statement: The icon is compiled into the binary rather than read at run time.
The menu opens the log file and the SavedVariables folder.
A SavedVariables folder under OneDrive is preferred over the folder under the profile.
Quitting kills the worker before the event loop exits.

value.definition: how the tray replaces its own executable from the server

invariants.statement: A replacement is triggered where the server's version differs from the built version.
The running executable is renamed aside before the downloaded executable takes that name.
The renamed old executable is deleted at the next start.
A replaced tray waits for the next login rather than restarting itself.
